skill.name: read-github
skill.description: Read GitHub repository documentation and code through GitMCP, with commands for fetching docs, searching docs, searching code, and retrieving referenced URLs.
skill.summary: Connect AI coding tools to GitMCP for repository documentation and code search.
skill.author: am-will

security_audit.summary: The Python helper has two real high-risk subprocess uses: it runs npx -y mcp-remote against input-derived MCP URLs. Most markdown backtick detections are false positives from documentation formatting, but the skill also allows arbitrary remote MCP endpoints, direct tool calls, and generic URL fetching through GitMCP. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the mcp-remote package version, remove -y auto-install, and require explicit user confirmation before starting remote MCP processes.
Validate repository input to GitHub owner/repo or GitHub URLs only, and reject other http or https endpoints.

remediation.issue: Direct tool and JSON argument forwarding
remediation.suggestion: Remove the generic call command, or restrict it to known GitMCP tool names derived from the selected repository.
Limit fetch-url to documented safe schemes and show the destination host before any fetch.
Document that repository identifiers and queries are sent to gitmcp.io, and advise users not to use private repository names.

semantic_findings.title: Arbitrary Remote MCP Endpoint Allowed
semantic_findings.description: Non-GitHub http inputs are returned unchanged by URL conversion and then passed to mcp-remote. A user or injected workflow could connect the helper to an arbitrary remote MCP server.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The conversion function only rewrites GitHub-style inputs and otherwise returns the original URL. Both subprocess call sites then pass that URL to mcp-remote.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted Direct MCP Tool Invocation
semantic_findings.description: The direct call command accepts an arbitrary tool name and JSON arguments, then forwards them to the selected MCP server. This broadens the skill beyond read-only repository helpers.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation advertises direct tool calls, and the CLI forwards user-provided tool names and parsed arguments without allowlisting.

semantic_findings.title: Generic URL Fetch Capability
semantic_findings.description: The skill exposes a fetch-url command that forwards user-supplied URLs to fetch_generic_url_content. This can retrieve arbitrary external content through GitMCP if the assistant follows untrusted documentation links.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both the skill instructions and CLI implementation expose a URL argument and pass it directly to GitMCP generic URL fetching.

content.value_statement: Teams need quick answers from repository docs and code without manual browsing. This skill connects Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to GitMCP repository search.
actual_capabilities: Converts GitHub URLs and owner/repo paths into GitMCP repository endpoints.
Lists available MCP tools for a selected repository.
Searches repository documentation semantically for a user query.
Searches repository code using the GitMCP code search tool.
Fetches referenced URL content through the GitMCP generic URL tool.
limitations: Requires network access and local execution of npx with mcp-remote.
Depends on gitmcp.io availability and the data it can access.
Does not include built-in authentication for private repositories.
Tool names depend on repository names generated by the GitMCP service.

use_cases.title: Understand a New Repository
use_cases.description: Fetch the README and documentation for a repository, then summarize the project purpose and setup steps.

use_cases.title: Find Documentation Details
use_cases.description: Search project documentation for installation, configuration, API behavior, or migration guidance.

use_cases.title: Locate Code References
use_cases.description: Search source code for exact names and connect implementation details back to documented behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Fetch Repository Overview
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the documentation for {owner}/{repo} and summarize the project purpose, installation steps, and first useful commands.

prompt_templates.title: Search Documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Search the documentation for {owner}/{repo} about {topic}. Return the most relevant sections and explain how they answer the question.

prompt_templates.title: Trace Code Usage
prompt_templates.prompt: Search code in {owner}/{repo} for {term}. Explain where it appears and how it relates to the documented feature.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Docs and Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch docs for {owner}/{repo}, search documentation for {topic}, then search code for related symbols. Report mismatches and open questions.

output_examples.input: Read facebook/react documentation and identify the best starting point for a new contributor.
output_examples.output: A concise overview of the project, key documentation pages, setup notes, and suggested next files to inspect.

output_examples.input: Search repository documentation for authentication configuration.
output_examples.output: A short list of relevant documentation matches, with explanations of each match and follow-up search terms.

output_examples.input: Find where the retry behavior is implemented.
output_examples.output: A summary of matching code locations, likely implementation files, and the relationship to documented behavior.

best_practices: Start with documentation fetch before targeted searches.
Use owner/repo paths or canonical GitHub URLs for repository input.
Review external URL destinations before using fetch-url.
anti_patterns: Do not use private repository names unless gitmcp.io use is approved.
Do not pass arbitrary MCP server URLs as repository input.
Do not use direct tool calls unless the tool name and arguments are trusted.

faq.question: Does this skill read private repositories?
faq.answer: It has no built-in authentication flow. Access depends on what GitMCP can reach and your local environment.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper connects to gitmcp.io through mcp-remote and uses external repository services.

faq.question: Can it search repository code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can call the GitMCP code search tool for exact-match code searches.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it install anything when used?
faq.answer: The helper runs npx -y mcp-remote, which may download the mcp-remote package if it is not already available.

faq.question: Can it fetch any URL?
faq.answer: It exposes fetch-url through GitMCP. Use it only for trusted URLs that are relevant to the repository task.
